title: Speculative Encoding: Many-to-Many Cache Translation
gist: One 2.35-billion-parameter network converts what a source model computed while reading a context into the form a different model needs, so the second model can continue without re-reading it. It covers seven open models of 8 to 14 billion parameters from four families, all 42 directions, where earlier translators needed one network per pair. A second network shrinks the translated cache to what a given question needs.
changes: The tracker's map rests on a cache belonging to one model, so a session stays on its first model. This attacks that tie. Inside a pool of open models a switch could cost a fraction of a re-read and a few points of accuracy. It does nothing across a closed model's API.
caveats: The authors' own results, on small models and multiple-choice questions over documents, with no agent sessions or tool calls. The loss grows with length, from 3% at 8,000 tokens to 17% at 128,000. Timings assume the source's side is already computed. It needs the source's internal states and the target's weights, so closed models are out. Code and weights came out in late November as a separate package.

numbers.metric: Accuracy kept with a translated cache, documents up to 8,000 tokens
numbers.value: 96.9% on average, 93.1% in the worst direction
numbers.baseline: the receiving model reading the text itself
numbers.setup: Seven models of 8 to 14 billion parameters, 42 directions, 12 tasks, three seeds

numbers.metric: Time to first token at 32,000 tokens
numbers.baseline: the receiving model re-reading the text
numbers.setup: One H200 with vLLM, the source's side already computed, median over 42 directions

numbers.metric: Time to first token at 128,000 tokens
numbers.value: 2.5x faster at 83% of accuracy; 6.1x and 7.5x for 1 to 2 points less with a shallower translator
numbers.baseline: the receiving model re-reading the text
numbers.setup: Documents 16 times longer than any used in training

numbers.metric: Translated cache shrunk for one question
numbers.value: up to 128x smaller within 2 points at 32,000 and 64,000 tokens; 4.3 points better at 128,000 and 64x

bears_on.note: Inside a pool of open models the cache need not pin a session to one model, if a few points of accuracy are acceptable. Across a closed model's API the claim's cache limit stands.
